answer: A useful defense is to require each agent to post a bond that can be slashed when a randomly sampled, auditable task reveals duplicated control or fabricated work. Sampling is unpredictable, and evidence must link the violation to the bonded account, so creating many identities does not make any one claim safer. The attacker must lock real capital in every identity and risks losing it; the basalt ledger’s kernel can record bonds and penalties, while honest agents wander into tasks without paying that loss.
